title: Spiced Minced Beef Keema with Potatoes
changes_from_base: Small potato cubes and a little water simmered with the tomatoes until tender; otherwise the same spice base and method.
summary: Aloo keema uses the classic keema spice base and method, with small potato cubes and a little water simmered alongside the tomatoes until tender. Hearty, warming and great with rolls or chapatis.
equipment: large saucepan or deep frying pan (24-28 cm) with lid

ingredients.item: large red onion, halved and thinly sliced
fine sea salt or table salt
Kashmiri chilli powder (or 1.5 tsp sweet paprika plus a pinch of cayenne)
waxy or all-rounder potatoes, peeled, cut into 1.5 cm cubes

steps.title: Flavour the oil
steps.text: This follows the classic keema, with potatoes simmered into the sauce. Heat the oil in the saucepan over medium heat and fry the peppercorns, cardamom and cinnamon for 30 seconds until aromatic, so their flavour infuses the oil.

steps.title: Deeply brown the onion
steps.text: Add the onion and cook, stirring, for 8-10 minutes until richly browned. This browning adds the sweetness that balances the spices.

steps.title: Fry the mince
steps.text: Stir the garlic and ginger through for 30 seconds before adding the mince and salt. Increase the heat to medium-high and cook for 8-12 minutes, breaking the meat into tiny pieces, until all the liquid has cooked off, the meat sizzles and the base of the pan is dry and browned.

steps.title: Stir in the spices
steps.text: Add the coriander, chilli powder, turmeric and cumin and cook for 1 minute, stirring, to toast them gently in the fat.

steps.title: Simmer the potatoes
steps.text: Add the tomatoes, yoghurt and green chilli along with the potatoes and water, and stir until simmering. Cover and cook over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the potatoes are tender when pierced with a knife, allowing 20-25 minutes, and a spoon drawn across the pan leaves a clear trail. The potatoes absorb the spiced sauce as they cook, and the small cubes soften in time with it.

steps.title: Check temperature
steps.text: Confirm that a thermometer pushed into the keema reads at least 71 °C before finishing.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Fish out the cinnamon stick and cardamom pods if you wish, stir in most of the coriander and top with the garam masala and remaining coriander. Bring to the table with the warm rolls and lime wedges.

tips: A common mistake is cutting the potatoes too large; keep them to 1.5 cm cubes so they cook through in the sauce.
Waxy or all-rounder potatoes hold their shape better than floury ones.
If the pan looks dry before the potatoes are tender, add a small splash of water and keep the lid on.
Stir gently near the end so the potato cubes stay whole.
storage: Cool within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat until piping hot (74 °C); freezing can make the potatoes grainy.
